chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a woman whose family claimed that she had made a will at the time of her death to free one of her slaves from one-third of her estate. He was asked: Is that slave freed, even though there is no witness to this except women? He said: 'The testimony of women is not valid in this matter.'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: And the reasoning in this narration is what we have mentioned in other narrations.
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of women valid for freeing a slave through a will in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) rules that the testimony of women is not valid for the specific matter of emancipating a slave via a will, distinguishing this financial bequest from other contexts. This ruling is contextualized within the broader Shia jurisprudential discussion on the admissibility of female witnesses in financial transactions, where their testimony is often considered sufficient but not equal to men's in certain evidentiary requirements. The hadith highlights the nuanced application of witness validity in Shia fiqh, particularly regarding the execution of wills and the liberation of slaves.
